questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

I started early from office, __lest I should not get caught__ in the rain.

options.text: lest I will not get caught

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'lest I should get caught'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here**, 'lest I should get caught'** should be used instead of **'lest I should not get caught'.**
 
• The **conjunction** '**lest**' means 'with the intention of preventing (something undesirable); to avoid the risk of.'
 
 
• *Example: He spent whole days in his room, wearing headphones **lest** he disturb anyone. *
 
 
 
• '**Lest**' is **a negative word.** Hence, the use of '**not**' after it is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The conjunction '**lest**' is usually followed by the '**should**' **modal**.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I started early from office, **lest I should get caught** in the rain*.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He has been talking / since two hours / and is still / not tired.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'since two hours'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'for two hours' **should be used instead of **'since two hours'.**
 
• **for + period: **a "**period**" is a duration of time -*** five minutes, two weeks, six years.***
 
• **'For'** means **"from the beginning of the period to the end of the period"**. 
 
• In the given sentence '**two hours**' is **a period of time.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *He has been talking **__for two hours__ **and is still not tired.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The preposition '**since**’ is **used for a point of time **and not a period of time.

 
 
• Example: We have lived here **since **1985.
